## Where datom is not a good fit. {#limits}

::: {style="margin-top: 1.1em; max-width: 40em; line-height: 1.45; font-size: 0.92em;"}
::: {.kicker}
By design
:::

- **Not a database.** No SQL engine, and not built for transactional, write-heavy work. It&rsquo;s for analytics: tables written when data changes, read many times.
- **Tables fit in memory.** Each table is processed in memory, so it should fit on a modern laptop. A set can span far more.
- **Flat tables.** Columns hold plain values, not nested lists.

::: {.kicker style="margin-top: 1em;"}
For now
:::

- **Languages:** writes from R; a Python reader is in preview.
- **Maturity:** 0.2.0 and experimental; the API can still change.
- **Where it runs:** a filesystem or S3 for data; GitHub, including Enterprise, for code.
:::

::: {.lede style="margin-top: 1.1em; max-width: 40em; font-size: 0.78em;"}
On validation: as with every R package, it&rsquo;s risk-based and done by each adopter, for their intended use. datom runs inside your SCE, not in place of it.
:::

::: notes
0:50
